Plants need sunlight for photosynthesis. Without light, a plant cannot grow well.
Sunlight helps a plant make food.
A plant without light often becomes weak and yellow.
What color are the leaves of most plants?
Red
Blue
Green
Yellow
Most leaves are green because they contain chlorophyll, which takes in sunlight.
Chlorophyll helps a plant make food from light.
In fall, leaves change color as chlorophyll breaks down.
What is the state of matter of water from a faucet?
Dry powder that does not flow
Tap water is a liquid. You can pour it, drink it, and wash with it.
Heating or cooling water can change its state.
Which material is hard and strong?
Dry sponge
Soft wax
Stone
Soft rubber
Stone is hard and strong. People use it for building and for heavy work.
Different materials have different properties, such as hardness or softness.
Stone is a natural material from Earth.
Which material is soft?
Metal
Cotton
Thin glass
Cotton is soft, so it is often used to make comfortable clothes.
Soft materials feel gentle to the touch.
Cotton comes from the cotton plant.
Which statement correctly describes a solid material?
A solid holds its own shape and does not flow.
A solid flows freely, like water.
A solid is always made from water.
A solid is always made of metal.
A solid material has a fixed shape. Unlike liquids, solids do not flow or pour — they hold their shape on their own.
Solids are one of the main states of matter.
Solids can be hard or soft, but they always keep their shape.
What can you usually see in the sky during the day?
Only the Moon, which belongs in the nighttime sky.
The Sun, and sometimes the Moon as well.
Stars shine just as brightly during the day as they do at night.
Only planets and water droplets high in the atmosphere.

The Sun lights up the daytime sky. Sometimes the Moon is also visible during the day, especially when it is in a phase where part of its lit surface faces Earth. Stars are always in the sky but are too faint to see when the Sun is up.
The Sun is our closest star and provides the light and warmth that make life possible.
The Moon orbits Earth and can sometimes be spotted during daylight hours.
What can you see in the sky at night?
The Sun — it shines in the sky both during the day and at night.
The Moon and stars.
The Moon, but no stars are ever visible.
Stars only — the Moon is never seen at night.

At night, the side of Earth you are on faces away from the Sun. Without the Sun's bright glare, you can see the Moon and stars. The Moon reflects sunlight, and stars are distant suns that produce their own light.
The Moon is visible at night because it reflects light from the Sun toward Earth.
Stars are always in the sky, but they can only be seen clearly when it is dark.
How does weather change?
It stays the same all year
It changes: hot, cold, rainy, or sunny
It stays hot everywhere on the same day
It stays cold with no warm days
Weather changes from day to day—hot or cold, rain, sun, wind, and more.
Weather can change from one day to the next.
The seasons are summer, winter, fall, and spring.
When does the Sun shine?
The Sun always shines—we see it by day when clouds do not block it
The Sun shines only at night
The Sun turns on and off each day
The Sun is not related to day and night
The Sun shines all the time. Clouds can hide it, so daylight may look dimmer.
The Sun keeps shining even when clouds cover the sky.
Clouds can block our view of the Sun.
What is the best way to deal with used materials to protect the environment?
Throw everything in the trash without sorting it.
Always buy brand-new materials instead of reusing old ones.
Reduce, reuse, or send materials to recycling.
Burn all waste materials at home to get rid of them.
Reducing, reusing, and recycling materials helps protect the environment by creating less waste and saving natural resources.
Reducing how much we use is the most effective way to help the environment.
Recycling saves resources and helps reduce pollution.
What helps keep the environment clean?
Cleaning only your house and leaving shared streets as they are
Putting trash in a bin instead of throwing it on the street
Collecting bottles in the yard and delaying pickup until spring
Packing trash until the bag tears before putting it in a bin
Putting trash in a bin—not on the street—helps keep places clean and pleasant.
Everyone can help keep the environment clean.
A cleaner environment is healthier and nicer for people.
Where should you throw trash?
In a trash bin or the right recycling container
Anywhere outdoors
Buried anywhere in the ground
Only into water
Trash belongs in a bin so the environment stays clean.
Trash bins are meant for collecting waste.
Using bins helps keep places clean and pleasant.
What should you do before starting an experiment?
Start mixing materials without reading labels
Decide what to test, plan the steps, and be careful
Do the hands-on steps before writing what you are testing
Decide the expected result without measuring first
Before an experiment, plan what you will test and stay safe. An adult should help.
Experiments should be done safely.
An adult should help with science experiments.
What is the main goal of a science experiment?
To make up interesting stories about materials.
To test an idea and find out what happens when you change something.
To list as many materials as possible without testing them.
To write down results before carrying out any test.
A science experiment allows you to test an idea and discover what happens under different conditions by observing and recording results.
Every experiment starts with a question or idea to test.
Experiments help us learn by testing ideas carefully and fairly.
What is chlorophyll?
A structural protein in the cell wall that only moves water
A green pigment in leaves that takes in light for making food
A wax layer on a leaf that fully blocks all leaf openings
A filling liquid between cells that has no pigment
Chlorophyll is the green material in leaves that takes in sunlight for photosynthesis.
Chlorophyll gives leaves their green color.
It is found in chloroplasts inside leaf cells.
What is the job of flowers?
Color and scent with no link to seeds or pollination
Attracting insects, pollination, and making seeds
Taking water from soil directly through the petals
Casting fixed shade on the stem with no role in reproduction
Flowers attract insects that move pollen. After that, seeds can form and grow into new plants.
Bright flowers help attract insects.
Insects help move pollen from flower to flower.
What is pollination?
When a plant dies at the end of winter
When pollen moves from one flower to another so seeds can form
When a plant burns in a forest fire
When a flower blooms before any pollen exists
Pollination is the transfer of pollen, often by insects, wind, or other animals. It helps plants make seeds and grow new plants.
Many flowers attract insects that carry pollen.
Without pollination, many plants cannot make seeds.
What happens when water is heated to a very high temperature?
It turns into a solid, like ice.
It turns into water vapor, which is a gas.
It stays liquid no matter how hot it gets.
It always turns into a hard solid material.
When water is heated to its boiling point, it changes state and becomes water vapor — a gas. This process is called evaporation or boiling.
Water can exist as a solid (ice), liquid (water), or gas (water vapor).
Heating gives water molecules enough energy to escape into the air as gas.
What is a conductor?
A material that does not carry electricity
A material that carries heat or electricity
A material that is always very hard
A material that is usually transparent
A conductor lets heat or electricity pass through easily. Metals are good conductors.
Metals such as copper and iron are good conductors.
Insulators such as wood or plastic do not carry electricity well.
What is an insulator?
A material that carries electricity well
A material that does not carry heat or electricity well
An insulator does not carry heat or electricity well. That helps keep heat in or prevent shocks.
Wood, plastic, and glass are common insulators.
Insulators are important for safety.
What causes the seasons?
Earth's distance from the Sun as the only cause.
Earth's tilt and its orbit around the Sun.
Day-to-day temperature swings in the weather.
Wind speed around Earth.

Earth is tilted on its axis and travels around the Sun over the course of a year. When a hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it receives more direct sunlight over more hours each day — producing summer. When it tilts away, it receives less direct sunlight — producing winter.
When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it experiences summer while the Southern Hemisphere has winter.
Earth's distance from the Sun changes only slightly during the year and is not the main cause of seasons.
What is the water cycle?
Rain falling to the sea with no evaporation returning to the air
The repeated movement of water among ocean, land, and air
Evaporation from the sea with no precipitation returning
Clouds that stay at one height forever
In the water cycle, water evaporates, forms clouds, falls as rain or snow, and returns to oceans and land.
The Sun heats water and drives evaporation.
Water keeps moving through this cycle.
What does weather describe?
Only the ocean temperature far from land
Day-to-day conditions of the air around us, such as hot, cold, rainy, or sunny
Only the rocks deep under Earth's surface
Only the positions of planets in the solar system
Weather is the day-to-day condition of the air outdoors — how hot or cold it is, whether it is rainy or sunny, and how windy it feels.
Weather can change from morning to night and from day to day.
Climate describes the usual weather pattern in a place over many years.
What is recycling?
Burying everything in backyard soil with no sorting
Using old materials again to make new products
Piling waste forever in one place with no recycling
Crushing mixed materials together with no prep for reuse
Recycling turns used materials such as plastic, paper, and glass into new products instead of throwing them away.
Recycling helps protect the environment.
It reduces waste and saves resources.
What is pollution?
An environment that is completely free of harmful materials
Adding harmful materials to the environment that cause damage
Rain that always washes every pollutant out of the air
Sunlight that fully blocks gases from entering the atmosphere
Pollution means harmful materials in air, water, or soil that can hurt animals, plants, and people.
Pollution can come from chimneys, cars, or trash.
It can harm nature and human health.
What is environmental conservation?
Developing wild land without checking effects on local species
Protecting nature, animals, and plants
Collecting litter outdoors only for display, not for recycling
